question: The book "Wings of Fire" is an autobiography of?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Abdul Kalam**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• **Wings of Fire** is the celebrated autobiography of **Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam**, who served as the **11th President of India** from **2002** to **2007**. It was originally published in **1999**.

• The book was co-authored by **Arun Tiwari** and provides a detailed account of **Dr. Kalam’s** journey from a humble childhood in **Rameswaram**, **Tamil Nadu**, to becoming a leading scientist in **India’s** space and missile programs.

• The narrative focuses on his early life, hardships, and his pivotal role at the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** and the **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)**.

• It highlights his leadership in the development of the **Satellite Launch Vehicle (SLV-3)** and the **Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme (IGMDP)**, which produced missiles like **Agni** and **Prithvi**.

• Since the book is a personal narrative of his own life and professional struggles, it is classified as an **autobiography**. Hence, the option **Abdul Kalam** is the correct answer.

**Additional Information__**

__

• **Vikram Seth**: He is a renowned **Indian** novelist and poet. He is best known for his epic novel **'A Suitable Boy'**, published in **1993**, and the verse novel **'The Golden Gate'**. He has received numerous awards, including the **Padma Shri** and the **Sahitya Akademi Award**. He is not the author of **Wings of Fire**.

• **R.K. Laxman**: **Rasipuram Krishnaswami Laxman** was a famous **Indian** cartoonist and illustrator. He is widely recognized for his creation **'The Common Man'** and his daily cartoon strip **'You Said It'** in **The Times of India**. His autobiography is titled **'The Tunnel of Time'**, published in **1998**.

• **C.V. Raman**: **Sir Chandrasekhara Venkata Raman** was a physicist who won the **Nobel Prize in Physics** in **1930** for his discovery of the **Raman Effect** (scattering of light), which he demonstrated on **28 February 1928**. This day is celebrated as **National Science Day** in **India**.

• **Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam** is often referred to as the **'Missile Man of India'** due to his immense contribution to the development of ballistic missile technology. He also played a key organizational and technical role in the **Pokhran-II** nuclear tests in **May 1998**.

**Important Points__**

• **Awards and Honors**: **Dr. Kalam** was honored with the **Bharat Ratna**, **India’s** highest civilian award, in **1997**. He also received the **Padma Bhushan** in **1981** and the **Padma Vibhushan** in **1990**.

• **Literary Works**: Apart from **Wings of Fire**, he authored several influential books, including **'India 2020: A Vision for the New Millennium'** (**1998**), **'Ignited Minds'** (**2002**), **'Indomitable Spirit'**, and **'Turning Points: A Journey Through Challenges'**.

• **Legacy**: **Dr. Kalam** passed away on **27 July 2015** while delivering a lecture at **IIM Shillong**. His birthday, **15 October**, is recognized by many institutions as **World Students Day** to honor his dedication to education and students.

• **Book Structure**: **Wings of Fire** is divided into four sections: **Orientation**, **Creation**, **Propitiation**, and **Contemplation**, representing different phases of his life and career.

50:T
